To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

pre service teachers' aims in practical work are based on the epistemology underlying the discovery and inquiry based science teaching approaches, and these aims are based on some epistemological problems.

pre service chemistry teachers are not aware of the epistemological issues related to the aims of using practical work in school chemistry and that these teachers should be taught about the nature of scientific knowledge, the nature of science teaching approaches, and the epistemological implications of the aims of using the practical work.
the main epistemological problem underlying pre service chemistry teacher's aims to use practical works in school science was the lack of an explicit understanding of the nature of science.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the epistemological basis underlying the use of the practical work in school chemistry, and the epistemological nature of the practical work itself.
the epistemological issues related to the aims of pre service chemistry teachers in using the practical work in science education.
the relationship between the epistemological views of pre service chemistry teachers and the aims they have in using practical work in science teaching.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the epistemological beliefs and the teaching approaches that pre service chemistry teachers had before they started the course on the nature of science and scientific inquiry were not changed by the course, and that these teachers still had epistemological problems in their aims to use the practical work in school chemistry
pre service chemistry teachers should be informed about the epistemological nature of practical work in order to be able to use it effectively and appropriately.

the epistemological problem is not only about what the nature of science is and how to teach it but also about how the nature of science should be used when teaching science and how it should be used in the teaching of science teaching approaches.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the pre service chemistry teachers who participated in this study were not able to use practical work to achieve some of their aims because of some epistemological problems that are related to their views about scientific knowledge, the nature of science and science teaching approaches.
the epistemological issues underlying some of the aims of pre service chemistry teachers to use practical work should be considered in teacher preparation programmes.
pre service teachers' aims for using practical work in school chemistry are not always in line with the epistemological nature of practical work.
The main takeaway from our work is that

pre service chemistry teachers should be made aware of the epistemological issues related to practical work and scientific inquiry in school science and that these should be discussed in teacher training programs.
the epistemological nature of practical work should be considered when teaching the science approaches and using the practice in school science.
the epistemology underlying the aims to use practical activities in school science should be explicitly considered in teacher education programs.
